title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
summary: Benchmark of multi-turn conversations between an LLM-simulated user and a tool-using agent bound by domain policy documents (retail, airline); success is judged by comparing the final database state with an annotated goal state, and pass^k measures reliability over repeated trials.
relation_to_specdx: τ-bench is one of SpecDx's subjects: its policy text is T and its goal-state/expected-action checks are C. τ-bench treats S as ground truth; SpecDx asks when the goal state itself is defective, and its repeated-trial (pass^k) runs are exactly the population of executions SpecDx mines.

title: τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
summary: Extends τ-bench with a telecom domain modelled as a Dec-POMDP in which both agent and user act on a shared world, a compositional generator that builds verifiable tasks from atomic components, and a user simulator constrained by the environment; it also fixes airline and retail tasks.
relation_to_specdx: Its airline and retail policies and task checks are SpecDx's second subject. The compositional task generator is a form of scenario synthesis, but it assumes the policy and checks are correct; SpecDx diagnoses defects in them (cf. the later τ²-Bench-Verified repairs).

title: WorkArena: How Capable are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?
venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2024), PMLR 235:11642-11662
summary: Introduces WorkArena, 33 tasks on the ServiceNow enterprise platform that knowledge workers routinely perform, together with the BrowserGym environment for web agents, and reports a large gap between open and closed LLMs.
relation_to_specdx: An enterprise-workflow benchmark whose task validators are hand-written checks (C) over a real business platform; it assumes them correct, whereas SpecDx would audit such validators against the task text.

venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37 (NeurIPS 2024), Datasets and Benchmarks Track
summary: WorkArena++ adds 682 compositional ServiceNow workflow tasks that test planning, arithmetic reasoning, retrieval and contextual understanding of web agents, compares LLMs/VLMs with human workers, and can generate ground-truth traces automatically.
relation_to_specdx: Compositional enterprise tasks with programmatic validators, a realistic setting where SpecDx-style auditing of validators against task descriptions could be applied; the paper does not question its validators.

title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
summary: AppWorld provides an execution engine of 9 everyday apps (457 APIs) populated with simulated users and a benchmark of 750 tasks requiring interactive code generation, evaluated by state-based unit tests that also check for collateral damage.
relation_to_specdx: Its programmatic state checks are clauses C in SpecDx's sense, including 'no collateral change' checks that can be weak or over-strict; AppWorld assumes they are correct, SpecDx would test them with a population of agents.

title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
summary: TheAgentCompany is an extensible benchmark that simulates a small software company with internal websites and simulated colleagues, and measures how far LLM agents can autonomously complete consequential professional tasks, with checkpoint-based partial credit.
relation_to_specdx: A business-workflow benchmark with checkpoint evaluators (C); context for SpecDx's claim that agent benchmarks treat their checks as ground truth.

title: ToolSandbox: A Stateful, Conversational, Interactive Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Tool Use Capabilities
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2025
summary: ToolSandbox evaluates tool-using LLMs with stateful tool execution, implicit state dependencies between tools, an on-policy user simulator, and a dynamic evaluation over intermediate and final milestones on arbitrary trajectories.
relation_to_specdx: Milestones/minefields are executable clauses over trajectories, similar to SpecDx's C; ToolSandbox does not diagnose whether milestones are mis-specified.

venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024

relation_to_specdx: Studies how agents read a workflow specification (T) in different formats; SpecDx inverts the question and uses agents' readings to find where the workflow specification itself is defective.

title: SOP-Bench: Complex Industrial SOPs for Evaluating LLM Agents
summary: SOP-Bench contains 2,000+ tasks derived from expert-written standard operating procedures in 12 business domains, with AI-generated, human-validated tools, APIs and datasets that give executable interfaces and ground-truth outputs.
relation_to_specdx: Its SOPs (T) and ground-truth outputs (C) were partly generated by AI and then validated by humans, which is exactly the kind of S that can carry defects SpecDx targets.

title: SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints
summary: SOPBench turns service-specific SOP code programs into directed graphs of executable functions across seven customer-service domains; agents must follow the natural-language SOP, the original code acts as a rule-based oracle verifier, and an automated generator produces 900+ verified test cases.
relation_to_specdx: Closest benchmark design to SpecDx's setting: NL SOP (T) paired with executable verifier code (C) and generated scenarios (Π). SOPBench assumes the code oracle matches the text; SpecDx tests that assumption and localises mismatches.

title: CRMArena: Understanding the Capacity of LLM Agents to Perform Professional CRM Tasks in Realistic Environments
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
summary: CRMArena is a benchmark of nine customer-service tasks over a realistic Salesforce-style CRM environment with 16 interconnected business objects, designed with CRM experts, on which state-of-the-art agents perform poorly.
relation_to_specdx: A sales/service business environment close to the TonomyX procurement/sales case; its ground-truth answers are taken as correct, whereas SpecDx would audit them.

title: CRMArena-Pro: Holistic Assessment of LLM Agents Across Diverse Business Scenarios and Interactions
summary: CRMArena-Pro extends CRMArena with 19 expert-validated tasks across sales, service and configure-price-quote processes for B2B and B2C, multi-turn persona-driven interactions and confidentiality-awareness assessment; leading agents reach about 58% single-turn success.
relation_to_specdx: Covers the sales/quote processes of TonomyX's domain; a candidate subject on which SpecDx's diagnosis could be run, but it does not itself analyse specification defects.

title: ST-WebAgentBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Safety and Trustworthiness in Web Agents
summary: ST-WebAgentBench pairs enterprise web tasks with explicit safety and trustworthiness policies scored on six dimensions, and introduces Completion-under-Policy, which credits only completions that respect all policies, plus a Risk Ratio of breaches.
relation_to_specdx: Policies are explicit clauses checked over agent behaviour, as in SpecDx's C; the benchmark measures agents against them, while SpecDx asks whether the policy clauses themselves are contradictory, hidden or weak.

title: IntellAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Conversational AI Systems
summary: IntellAgent is an open-source multi-agent framework that builds a graph of policies (nodes weighted by complexity, edges by co-occurrence), samples multi-policy events and user goals from it, simulates user-agent dialogues and critiques the agent's policy adherence for fine-grained diagnostics.
relation_to_specdx: Shares SpecDx's policy-driven scenario generation and fine-grained per-policy diagnosis, but its goal is to diagnose the agent and it treats the policy as correct; SpecDx diagnoses the policy/check pair from a population of agents.
baseline_notes: Inputs: the policy text T (τ²-bench airline/retail policy or TonomyX requirement documents) plus tool schemas and a database. IntellAgent builds a policy graph and samples multi-policy scenarios with expected behaviour; adapting it, we would (i) replace SpecDx's Thompson-sampling scenario synthesiser with IntellAgent's policy-graph sampler as an ablation of component 6, and (ii) use its critique agent's per-policy verdicts over our agent runs as a single-judge defect detector. Code: Apache-2.0, Python, LangGraph; it can run with local models through LangChain, so offline use is feasible.

title: WorkBench: a Benchmark Dataset for Agents in a Realistic Workplace Setting
verified_by: proceedings page https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/329746 (COLM 2024, OpenReview forum 4HNAwZFDcH); arXiv 2405.00823
summary: WorkBench is a sandbox with five business databases, 26 tools and 690 workplace tasks whose success is judged by comparing the resulting database state with a unique ground-truth outcome (outcome-centric evaluation).
relation_to_specdx: Outcome-centric evaluation is the 'golden end state' clause type in SpecDx's C. WorkBench asserts each outcome is unique and unambiguous; SpecDx's ambiguity type tests exactly that assertion.

title: WorkBench Revisited: Workplace Agents Two Years On
summary: Revisits WorkBench two years on: frontier agents now complete 98% of tasks and make far fewer harmful actions, and the authors release an updated benchmark with data and code quality improvements.
relation_to_specdx: Illustrates that benchmark specifications need repair over time ('data and code quality improvements'), the maintenance task SpecDx automates.

title: Action-Based Conversations Dataset: A Corpus for Building More In-Depth Task-Oriented Dialogue Systems
venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies
summary: ABCD is a corpus of over 10K human-to-human customer-service dialogues with 55 intents, each requiring a sequence of actions constrained by explicitly defined company policies; it introduces Action State Tracking and Cascading Dialogue Success tasks.
relation_to_specdx: An early dataset that operationalises business-policy adherence for agents, a predecessor of τ-bench's policy documents; it does not analyse defects in the guidelines.

title: Beyond IVR: Benchmarking Customer Support LLM Agents for Business-Adherence
summary: JourneyBench uses graph representations of support workflows to generate customer-support scenarios and measures policy adherence with a User Journey Coverage Score, comparing a static-prompt agent with a dynamic-prompt agent that explicitly models policy control.
relation_to_specdx: Graph-based scenario generation from business policies resembles SpecDx's scenario synthesis; it scores agents, not the policy graph.

title: CompliBench: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Compliance Violation Detection in Dialogue Systems
summary: CompliBench evaluates whether LLM judges can detect and localise guideline violations in multi-turn agent dialogues, using an automated pipeline with controllable flaw injection that yields ground-truth labels of the violated guideline and turn.
relation_to_specdx: Its controllable flaw injection with exact ground truth parallels SpecDx's mutation operators, but flaws are injected into agent behaviour, not into the specification; LLM-judge verdicts are a possible single-judge baseline.

title: Effective Red-Teaming of Policy-Adherent Agents
summary: Proposes a threat model of adversarial users exploiting policy-adherent customer-service agents, the CRAFT multi-agent red-teaming system using policy-aware persuasion, and τ-break, a τ-bench extension for robustness to manipulative users.
relation_to_specdx: Uses τ-bench policies as the fixed reference and attacks agents; complementary to SpecDx, which questions the policy and checks rather than the agent's robustness.

title: Establishing Best Practices in Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025), Datasets and Benchmarks Track
summary: Shows that many agentic benchmarks have flaws in task setup or reward design (e.g., τ-bench counting empty responses as success), which can mis-estimate performance by up to 100% relative, and proposes the Agentic Benchmark Checklist (ABC) for task and outcome validity.
relation_to_specdx: Documents weak checks and task defects in τ-bench, supporting SpecDx's motivation; the diagnosis is manual (expert checklist), whereas SpecDx is automatic and typed.

title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: A Validity Audit of Tool-Calling Evaluation
summary: Audits four tool-calling benchmark families (BFCL v4, τ²-Bench, LiveMCPBench, MCP-Atlas) over 496 expert-reviewed tasks, finding an 18.5% evaluator-human disagreement rate caused by brittle state matching, trajectory lock-in, incorrect ground truths and judge drift, and releases a failure taxonomy and corrected evaluators.
relation_to_specdx: Provides human-audited real defects in τ²-Bench that can serve as SpecDx ground truth and a taxonomy to map onto contradiction/hidden requirement/ambiguity/weak check; its audit is manual, SpecDx's is automatic.

title: MANTRA: Synthesizing SMT-Validated Compliance Benchmarks for Tool-Using LLM Agents
summary: MANTRA synthesises machine-checkable compliance benchmarks from natural-language procedural manuals and tool schemas: it separately generates a symbolic world model and trace-level compliance checks, validates their mutual consistency with SMT solving, repairs inconsistencies in a loop, and derives tasks of tunable complexity.
relation_to_specdx: Threatens part of SpecDx's novelty: it automatically detects inconsistencies between NL-derived checks and a model of the manual using a solver. It differs in that it validates checks it generated itself, uses no population of executors, and gives no typed diagnosis of ambiguity or weak checks in a pre-existing specification.

title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering
summary: AgentSpec is a lightweight DSL for runtime constraints on LLM agents: rules combine triggers, predicates and enforcement actions, and are applied to code-execution, embodied and autonomous-driving agents with millisecond overhead; LLM-generated rules are also evaluated.
relation_to_specdx: AgentSpec rules are executable clauses like SpecDx's guardrail triggers; it enforces them as given, while SpecDx asks whether such rules are contradictory, too strict or too weak relative to the text.

title: ProbGuard: Proactive Runtime Monitoring for LLM Agent Safety via Probabilistic Prediction
venue: Proceedings of the 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
summary: ProbGuard abstracts agent executions into symbolic states, learns a discrete-time Markov chain from traces, and proactively intervenes when the predicted probability of reaching an unsafe state exceeds a threshold, with PAC-style guarantees on the estimates.
relation_to_specdx: Like SpecDx it learns a statistical model from many agent traces, but it uses it to predict and prevent agent violations of a trusted specification rather than to diagnose the specification.

venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2025), PMLR 267:8313-8344
summary: ShieldAgent extracts verifiable rules from policy documents, organises them into action-based probabilistic rule circuits, and checks a protected agent's trajectory against them with formal verification tools; it introduces ShieldAgent-Bench with 3,000 instruction/trajectory pairs.
relation_to_specdx: It compiles NL policy (T) into checkable rules (C) automatically, the step whose errors SpecDx detects; it does not examine whether extracted rules conflict with or under-approximate the policy text.

title: Towards Enforcing Company Policy Adherence in Agentic Workflows
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
summary: Compiles company policy documents offline into verifiable guard code attached to each tool, and runs the guards before each agent action at runtime, giving deterministic and transparent policy enforcement; demonstrated on the τ-bench airline domain.
relation_to_specdx: Works on exactly SpecDx's τ-bench airline subject and makes T executable as guards, but trusts the policy and the compilation; SpecDx's comparison of T, C and agent behaviour would expose where ToolGuard's guards and the benchmark checks disagree.
baseline_notes: Inputs: the policy document T and tool schemas (τ-bench airline policy is its own evaluation domain). Its buildtime stage compiles each policy into Python guard functions per tool. As a baseline: compile T into guards, then (a) compare guards against the benchmark's checks C to flag clauses that no guard justifies (hidden requirement) or guards that no clause enforces (weak check), and (b) run the guards on the agent population's traces. Code: open source at github.com/AgentToolkit/toolguard (Apache-2.0, Python, pushed 2026-08; referenced by Langflow's Policies component), runnable with any LangChain-compatible LLM, so offline use with local models is feasible.

title: Solver-Aided Verification of Policy Compliance in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
summary: Translates natural-language tool-use policies into SMT-LIB constraints with an LLM-assisted, human-guided process; at runtime each planned tool call is checked with Z3 as a precondition and blocked if it violates the policy; evaluated on τ-bench with fewer violations at unchanged task accuracy.
relation_to_specdx: Shares SpecDx's use of solvers over τ-bench policy clauses, but for enforcement on agents; it does not use the solver to test the policy/check pair for contradictions or looseness.
baseline_notes: Inputs: NL tool-use policy (τ-bench airline/retail policy text). It translates policies into SMT-LIB constraints over agent-observable state and tool arguments and checks planned tool calls with Z3. As a baseline for SpecDx's B5 (symbolic analysis without interpreters): conjoin the formalised policy constraints with the benchmark's checks C and query Z3 for unsatisfiability (contradiction) or for models that satisfy C but violate the policy (weak check). Code status: not found in the abstract; translation is LLM-assisted with human guidance, so a fully automatic run needs the LLM step only.

title: Enforcing Temporal Constraints for LLM Agents
venue: arXiv preprint (ICLR 2026 Workshop VerifAI-2, per project listing)
summary: Agent-C offers a DSL for temporal safety properties of agent actions (e.g., authenticate before accessing data), translates them to first-order logic, uses SMT solving during token generation to detect non-compliant tool calls, and constrains decoding to compliant alternatives; evaluated on retail and airline customer-service domains.
relation_to_specdx: Formalises τ-bench-style retail/airline rules as temporal constraints; it assumes the rules are right and makes agents obey them, whereas SpecDx checks whether such rules and the benchmark checks are mutually consistent and faithful to T.

title: AgentLTL: A Trace-Verification Framework for Measuring, Enforcing, and Training Procedural Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
summary: AgentLTL is a first-order LTL-derived language for procedural rules over agent traces that yields a deterministic, judge-free compliance score, used both to gate tool calls online and as a dense reward for fine-tuning.
relation_to_specdx: Gives a trace-level clause language like SpecDx's C; it scores agents against the clauses, while SpecDx scores the clauses against a population of agents.

title: Symbolic Temporal Supervision of LLM Agents Using Contracts
summary: ContrAgent formalises an agent's tool-call trace over checkable predicates and specifies required behaviour as assume-guarantee contracts in LTLf compiled to DFAs, used both for online gating and offline trace evaluation.
relation_to_specdx: Contract libraries are another form of executable clause set C; contract consistency checking (assume-guarantee) is a symbolic B5-style analysis without interpreters.

title: Policy-as-Prompt: Turning AI Governance Rules into Guardrails for AI Agents
venue: 3rd Regulatable ML Workshop at NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv preprint)
summary: Converts unstructured design artifacts (PRDs, technical design documents, code) and risk controls into a source-linked policy tree that is compiled into prompt-based classifiers for runtime monitoring of agents, with provenance and human review.
relation_to_specdx: Derives guardrails C from requirement documents T with traceability links, the T-to-C mapping that SpecDx audits; it does not test the derived guardrails for defects.

title: Autoformalization of Agent Instructions into Policy-as-Code
venue: Second Workshop on Agents in the Wild (AIWILD) at ICML 2026 (arXiv preprint)
summary: Translates agent prompts, MCP tool descriptions and natural-language policy documents into formally verified Cedar policies with an LLM generator-critic loop, covering more of the source specification on MedAgentBench than hand-coded symbolic enforcement.
relation_to_specdx: Measures how much of T a formal policy covers, i.e., the hidden-requirement/weak-check gap between T and C that SpecDx detects statistically; its coverage is judged against the text, not via executor behaviour.

title: NeMo Guardrails: A Toolkit for Controllable and Safe LLM Applications with Programmable Rails
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations
summary: NeMo Guardrails is an open-source toolkit that adds user-defined, model-independent and interpretable programmable rails (e.g., topic restrictions, predefined dialogue paths) to LLM conversational systems through a runtime inspired by dialogue management.
relation_to_specdx: An industrial guardrail layer of the kind SpecDx's guardrail triggers model; context only.

title: PolicyGuard: A Dialogue-Grounded Sub-Agent Verifier for Policy Adherence in LLM Agents
venue: arXiv preprint (poster at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop 'Who Verifies the Agents?')
summary: PolicyGuard is a sub-agent verifier that shares the agent's dialogue view, intercepts mutating tool calls, reasons over the raw policy text in context and returns remediation feedback; on τ²-bench airline it raises pass^4 by 6-12 points across three vendors and transfers to retail and telecom.
relation_to_specdx: Evaluated on SpecDx's τ²-bench subject and reasons directly over the policy text T; it treats T as authoritative and fixes agents, so residual disagreements between PolicyGuard and the benchmark checks are candidate specification defects SpecDx would type.

title: Agentic Business Process Management: A research manifesto

title: Semantics, Analysis and Simplification of DMN Decision Tables
summary: Journal version: a formal semantics of DMN decision tables, a general geometric approach to analyse and refactor them, efficient algorithms for detecting overlapping and missing rules, and a table simplification by rule merging, evaluated on real and synthetic tables.
relation_to_specdx: The strongest symbolic baseline for rule-shaped clauses: it finds conflicts and gaps in C by geometry alone. SpecDx differs by relating C to the NL text T through executor readings, and by typing hidden requirements and weak checks that are invisible inside C alone.
baseline_notes: Inputs: decision tables (input intervals/enumerations to outputs). Adaptation: encode the rule-like parts of C (e.g., τ²-bench airline refund/cancellation eligibility, or TonomyX approval thresholds and SQL policy functions) as DMN tables over the clause variables, then run overlap detection (candidate ambiguity/contradiction among clauses) and missing-rule detection (inputs no clause decides, candidate weak checks). It needs a manual or LLM-assisted encoding of C into tables and sees only C, not T or agent behaviour. Code: the paper reports an implementation; no maintained public repository was verified, so a re-implementation of the geometric overlap/gap sweep (straightforward for interval inputs) is the practical route.

title: Resolving inconsistencies and redundancies in declarative process models
summary: Discovered Declare models can contain mutually contradicting constraints that accept no trace; the paper resolves such inconsistencies and removes redundancies automatically using automata products (an automata-product monoid), keeping the most interesting constraints while guaranteeing a consistent model.
relation_to_specdx: Directly addresses contradiction in a declarative clause set, i.e., SpecDx's contradiction type, with automata rather than sampled correction sets; it decides which constraints to drop by interest heuristics, not by evidence from executors or the NL text.
baseline_notes: Inputs: a Declare constraint set. Adaptation: express SpecDx's temporal clauses (e.g., 'verify identity before modifying a reservation', 'no refund after cancellation') as Declare/LTLf templates; the MINERful implementation then removes constraints until the set is satisfiable (yielding conflict sets comparable to SpecDx's candidate MUSes) and prunes redundant ones. Sees only C. Code: the technique is implemented in MINERful (Java, GPL-3.0; a repository exists at github.com/Process-in-Chains/MINERful, reached via the authors' account, but the paper itself was not checked for the link).

title: Measuring Inconsistency in Declarative Process Specifications
summary: Shows that classical inconsistency measures cannot assess inconsistency in LTL with temporal operators, proposes a paraconsistent semantics for LTL on fixed traces, and defines two inconsistency measures with desirable properties for declarative process specifications, with a complexity analysis.
relation_to_specdx: Quantifies how inconsistent a declarative specification is, with MUS-based measures among the baselines; SpecDx localises and types contradictions from behaviour and refutes candidates with witnesses, which these measures do not.
baseline_notes: Inputs: a set of LTL-on-fixed-traces formulas (declarative constraints). Adaptation: encode SpecDx's clause set C (temporal and state clauses for a scenario of bounded length) as LTLff, compute the paper's paraconsistent inconsistency measures to rank clause sets by degree of conflict and compare with SpecDx's contradiction scores. Code: per the authors' publication list, a follow-up ASP-based framework (Kuhlmann, Corea, Grant) implements satisfiability checking and two inconsistency measures; no repository was verified.
